name: Nebius Group
description: Nebius rents out AI computing capacity: GPU clusters in its own and leased data centres, with software on top, to AI labs, startups, enterprises and, since late 2025, two hyperscalers. Its core business is the Nebius AI cloud, which was 90 percent of 2025 revenue ($480 million of $530 million, up 603 percent) and turned Adjusted EBITDA-positive ($59 million) in 2025. Two long-term deals with Microsoft (up to $17.4 billion over five years, including about $7.0 billion of upfront payments) and Meta provide committed revenue. The group also owns the self-driving unit Avride and the coding-education business TripleTen, both loss-making, and holds stakes in ClickHouse and Toloka, which it spun out. Active power capacity was about 170 MW at year-end 2025, with over 2 GW contracted.

hq.note: Headquartered in Amsterdam (FY2025 20-F); Dutch N.V. The company was formerly Yandex N.V. (EDGAR filings before FY2024 carry the yndx name).

employees.note: "Approximately 1,500 employees, the majority of whom are engineers" (FY2025 20-F)

businessLines.name: Nebius AI cloud
businessLines.how: Customers pay for GPU capacity under long-term committed contracts (the Microsoft deal carries upfront payments plus monthly fees owed irrespective of utilisation), plus software and inference services; it builds and finances the data centres itself.
businessLines.description: Full-stack AI cloud: GPU compute clusters, storage, managed services and the Token Factory inference service, run from data centres in Europe, the US, the Middle East and elsewhere.

businessLines.name: TripleTen
businessLines.how: Revenue per enrolled student times enrolment; the 20-F attributes growth to enrolment and average revenue per student.
businessLines.description: Online coding and data bootcamps with career support.

businessLines.name: Avride
businessLines.how: Revenue is tiny ($1.3M) against an Adjusted EBITDA loss of $82.7M; the revenue model is not described in the text read.
